title: English Vocabulary 4 · Units 83–84
description: Advanced expressions for approximate quantities, conversational vagueness, vocal delivery, interaction styles and articulation.
sourceNotice: Prepared for personal study from the user-provided Advanced third-edition book. Original exercises and extended source passages are not reproduced.

audit.scope: Unit 83 and Unit 84 teaching pages, register and common-mistake notes, exercises 83.1–83.5 and 84.1–84.4, and corresponding answer-key entries. Exercise-only targets are flagged separately.
audit.pronunciation: Broad British IPA is supplied only for short targets where confidence is high; blank IPA is intentionally used for longer or uncertain expressions. IPA does not transcribe connected-speech detail.
audit.languagePolicy: Learner-facing fields and metadata are in English, except Brazilian Portuguese translations under pt.
audit.reviewMethod: Compared teaching and exercise targets with the uploaded Advanced third-edition PDF and answer key. Rechecked language register, natural collocations, separate senses, Portuguese translations and independently drafted examples. The saved JSON was parsed and checked for canonical keys and types, IDs, provenance and static word/sentence audio constraints.

units.title: Unit 83 — Give or take: more vague expressions
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 83. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Language use · approximation and conversational vagueness
learningObjectives: Qualify figures, durations and quantities using accurate formal or informal approximations.
Distinguish small and large quantities with natural collocations such as a smidgen of and stacks of.
Use conversational softeners and generalisers without confusing them with exact statements.
Recognise informal -ish/-y approximations and patterns used in everyday speech.

sectionsChecked: Full teaching page: A · Vague numbers and quantities, B · Softening precision and certainty, C · Additional conversational approximators
Facing exercise page and relevant answer-key entries
Common mistakes, source register notes and lexical contrasts where applicable

items.pt: mais de; acima de
items.example: The planned investment is in excess of three million pounds.
items.note: A relatively formal way to say that an amount is greater than a stated figure; common in financial or official writing.

items.pt: na faixa de; aproximadamente
items.example: The repairs are expected to cost in the region of eight thousand pounds.
items.note: Used before approximate figures or amounts, often where an exact estimate is unavailable.

items.pt: a mais ou a menos; com margem de variação
items.example: The journey takes four hours, give or take twenty minutes.
items.note: Informal; follows an estimate and introduces the possible amount by which it may differ.

items.pt: aproximadamente; cerca de
items.example: Approximately sixty per cent of the participants completed the survey.
items.note: Relatively formal alternative to about or around when reporting estimates.

items.pt: ou algo assim; aproximadamente
items.example: We should receive the results in a fortnight or so.
items.note: Informal approximation following a number, time period or amount; does not specify an exact margin.

items.pt: um bom número de; bastante gente/coisas
items.example: Quite a few applicants withdrew after seeing the job requirements.
items.note: Indicates a noticeably large number rather than just a few; can imply surprise or disappointment.

items.pt: uma pequena quantidade de; um punhado de
items.example: Only a smattering of local residents attended the consultation.
items.note: A small and scattered number or proportion; may suggest that representation is limited.

items.pt: uma pitada de; um pouquinho de (líquido ou tempero)
items.example: The dressing needs a dash of lemon juice.
items.note: A very small amount, especially of a flavouring or liquid ingredient.

items.pt: uma quantidade mínima de; um tiquinho de
items.example: There is a smidgen of doubt about the final estimate.
items.note: Informal word for a tiny quantity; can be used figuratively as well as with food.

items.pt: uma porção; uma colherada generosa de
items.example: Add a dollop of yoghurt to each bowl before serving.
items.note: A soft rounded portion of something such as cream, sauce or yoghurt; its size varies.

items.pt: um montão de; grandes quantidades de
items.example: We still have stacks of paperwork to complete before the inspection.
items.note: Informal expression meaning many or a lot; not necessarily a literal pile.

items.pt: mais ou menos; praticamente
items.example: The manuscript is more or less ready for publication.
items.note: Used with a verb or state to mean almost or essentially, without claiming absolute completion.

items.pt: mais ou menos; aproximadamente igual
items.example: The two solutions perform more or less equally well.
items.note: Used with comparisons to indicate broad similarity without exact equivalence.

items.pt: um pouco; meio
items.example: The instructions seem a bit unclear to new users.
items.note: Informal softener used before an adjective or adverb, sometimes mitigating a negative judgement.

items.pt: um certo; meio que um(a)
items.example: The delayed shipment became a bit of a headache for the team.
items.note: Precedes a singular countable noun phrase; often reduces the directness of a negative assessment.

items.pt: ou qualquer coisa do tipo; ou algo assim
items.example: After the talk, we could go for coffee or whatever.
items.note: Very informal way of keeping options open without listing every alternative.

items.pt: ou algo assim; ou alguma coisa do tipo
items.example: Could you bring a notebook or something to write on?
items.note: Informal way of suggesting an unspecified similar alternative.

items.pt: e coisas desse tipo
items.example: She enjoys pottery, sketching and things like that.
items.note: Used to extend a list to similar activities or objects without specifying them.

items.pt: e esse tipo de coisa
items.example: The club organises film nights, discussions and that kind of thing.
items.note: Conversational generaliser referring to more examples in the same broad category.

items.pt: algo nessa linha; algo semelhante
items.example: We need a flexible timetable or something along those lines.
items.note: Refers to a solution or suggestion roughly resembling what has just been described.

items.pt: palavras nesse sentido; algo desse teor
items.example: The manager said the plan was no longer viable, or words to that effect.
items.note: Signals an approximate paraphrase, not necessarily the speaker’s exact wording; useful when reporting speech.

items.pt: uma espécie de; um tipo de
items.example: The prototype has a sort of flexible hinge at one end.
items.note: A loose classification that avoids identifying something too precisely.

items.pt: meio que; mais ou menos; uma espécie de
items.example: The surface felt kind of rubbery when I touched it.
items.note: In conversation, can soften a description; a kind of also introduces a rough noun category.

items.pt: bem; então; bom (marcador de hesitação)
items.example: He is, well, not entirely convinced by the proposal.
items.note: A spoken discourse marker that signals hesitation, qualification or a search for a better word.

items.pt: de uns quarenta anos; quarenta e poucos
items.example: The person who answered the door looked fortyish.
items.note: A natural extension of the exercise’s age + -ish pattern; the suffix makes a number approximate.

items.pt: avermelhado; meio vermelho
items.example: The samples developed a reddish colour after exposure to heat.
items.note: The suffix -ish expresses an approximate colour or quality.

items.pt: meio elástico; com aparência ou textura elástica
items.example: There was an elasticky strip around the edge of the cover.
items.note: Playful, informal -y formation suggesting a quality rather than defining it precisely; not suitable for formal technical description.

items.pt: um pouco grande demais; para o lado do grande
items.example: The replacement cabinet is on the big side for our small office.
items.note: On the ... side evaluates a degree of a quality, often implying it exceeds what is ideal.

items.pt: e tal; e coisas do tipo
items.example: We spent the afternoon shopping and that.
items.note: Very informal addition meaning and similar activities or things; mainly conversational.

items.pt: e coisas do gênero; e semelhantes
items.example: The new service covers printing, binding and suchlike.
items.note: Informal generaliser following a list, often after plural or uncountable nouns.

items.pt: de um jeito ou de outro; de alguma forma
items.example: The revised rule will affect every department in one way or another.
items.note: Vague expression deliberately leaving the specific manner or mechanism unstated.

units.title: Unit 84 — The way you say it
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 84. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Language use · speaking style, tone and articulation
learningObjectives: Choose speech verbs that convey volume, pitch, emotion and communicative intent.
Distinguish quiet speech, loud speech, criticism, gossip, teasing and flattery.
Use idiomatic verb patterns with at, about and other prepositions.
Describe articulation and speech fluency accurately and respectfully.

sectionsChecked: Full teaching page: A · Loudness and vocal delivery, B · Conversation styles and intentions, C · Speech difficulties and articulation
Facing exercise page and relevant answer-key entries
Common mistakes, source register notes and lexical contrasts where applicable

items.pt: resmungar ou falar baixo e de maneira indistinta
items.example: He mumbled his answer so quietly that nobody understood it.
items.note: Speech is quiet or unclear because the sounds are not articulated distinctly; often disapproving.

items.pt: resmungar; murmurar entre dentes
items.example: She muttered a complaint as she left the meeting.
items.note: Low, often discontented speech, sometimes not intended for other people to hear.

items.pt: entre dentes; em voz muito baixa
items.example: He made a sarcastic remark under his breath.
items.note: Quietly enough not to be heard clearly, often because the speaker does not wish to be overheard.

items.pt: murmurar suavemente; dizer em voz baixa
items.example: The audience murmured in approval as the results were announced.
items.note: Soft, low speech or sound; unlike mutter, it can imply approval or calmness.

items.pt: sem reclamar; sem protestar
items.example: The volunteers accepted the revised schedule without a murmur.
items.note: Fixed expression meaning without complaint or protest, not literally without making a sound.

items.pt: aumentar o tom de voz; falar mais alto
items.example: Please raise your voice slightly so those at the back can hear you.
items.note: Can be a neutral request to speak louder; context determines whether it implies anger.

items.pt: levantar a voz com alguém; falar de maneira exaltada
items.example: She asked him not to raise his voice at the receptionist.
items.note: Raise your voice at someone usually refers to an angry or confrontational tone.

items.pt: falar mais alto; elevar a voz
items.example: Could you speak up so the audience can hear your question?
items.note: Common phrasal verb in a request to speak louder or more clearly; not necessarily angry.

items.pt: com dificuldade auditiva; que não ouve bem
items.example: Use the microphone so that visitors who are hard of hearing can follow the tour.
items.note: Respectful descriptive expression for having difficulty hearing; do not equate it with complete deafness.

items.pt: gritar com alguém
items.example: The supervisor should explain the mistake rather than shout at the intern.
items.note: Loud speech directed at somebody; shouting at someone may suggest anger.

items.pt: gritar com; berrar para
items.example: They had to yell at each other across the noisy station.
items.note: Can convey urgency, anger or the need to be heard over background noise.

items.pt: gritar estridentemente com
items.example: The frustrated customer screamed at the member of staff.
items.note: Very loud, intense voice; at introduces the person it is directed towards.

items.pt: bradar; rugir; gritar com voz profunda
items.example: The supporters roared when the final whistle sounded.
items.note: A powerful, deep, very loud sound; can express anger or excitement.

items.pt: soltar um grito agudo; guinchar
items.example: She shrieked with delight when she opened the envelope.
items.note: A loud, high-pitched cry, associated with excitement, fear or pain.

items.pt: bradar com; rugir para alguém
items.example: The coach roared at the players after the careless mistake.
items.note: Describes extremely loud, usually low-pitched speech directed at someone.

items.pt: gritar agudamente com
items.example: She shrieked at her brother when he startled her.
items.note: High-pitched voice directed at someone; very different in pitch from roar.

items.pt: pegar no pé; importunar com críticas repetidas
items.example: He keeps nagging his flatmate about leaving dishes in the sink.
items.note: Repeated criticism or reminders about someone’s behaviour or duties; nag someone about something.

items.pt: discutir por bobagens; ficar implicando um com o outro
items.example: The siblings bickered over whose turn it was to wash up.
items.note: Irritated argument about a small or unimportant matter.

items.pt: discutir por algo trivial; bater boca
items.example: The committee spent too long squabbling about minor details.
items.note: Similar to bicker: argue noisily about an insignificant issue.

items.pt: falar mal de alguém; detonar verbalmente
items.example: It was unprofessional to slag off former colleagues during the interview.
items.note: Very informal, strongly negative British expression for insulting or criticising someone.

items.pt: choramingar; reclamar de maneira irritante
items.example: He whined about the hotel breakfast for the entire journey.
items.note: Complain in a persistent, often high-pitched or childish manner.

items.pt: ficar se queixando; reclamar sem parar
items.example: Rather than whinge about the deadline, they decided to reorganise the work.
items.note: Informal, predominantly British: complain repeatedly and annoyingly.

items.pt: ficar batendo papo; conversar sem parar
items.example: They chatted away while waiting for the train.
items.note: Away suggests continuous or extended light conversation, rather than a single brief remark.

items.pt: fofocar; falar da vida alheia
items.example: The neighbours often gossip about people they barely know.
items.note: Talk about other people, often sharing private details or unverified stories.

items.pt: zoar; provocar; tirar sarro de alguém
items.example: They were only winding him up about his new hairstyle.
items.note: Informal; tease or deliberately mislead someone. Here wind is pronounced /waɪnd/, unlike the noun wind /wɪnd/.

items.pt: uma pegadinha; uma provocação; uma zoeira
items.example: The supposed prize announcement turned out to be a complete wind-up.
items.note: Informal noun for a practical joke or deliberate teasing; pronounce wind like /waɪnd/.

items.pt: bajular; adular para conseguir algo
items.example: He tried to butter up the director before asking for a favour.
items.note: Informal, negative: praise or flatter someone with a hidden self-interested purpose.

items.pt: exagerar; aumentar a importância de algo
items.example: The journalist exaggerated the significance of the preliminary findings.
items.note: Describe something as greater, worse or more important than it really is.

items.pt: exagero; distorção por exagero
items.example: Calling a minor delay a disaster was clearly an exaggeration.
items.note: Noun derived from exaggerate; the claim overstates reality.

items.pt: levar ao pé da letra; interpretar literalmente
items.example: Don’t take his description literally; he tends to exaggerate.
items.note: Interpret words according to their exact meaning, without allowing for humour, hyperbole or figurative intent.

items.pt: generalizar; tirar conclusões gerais
items.example: It is risky to generalise from a survey of just twelve people.
items.note: Make a broad statement from specific examples or limited evidence; British spelling generalise.

items.pt: generalização
items.example: The report makes a sweeping generalisation about consumer behaviour.
items.note: A broad claim presented as generally true; British spelling generalisation.

items.pt: ceceio; dificuldade de pronunciar certos sons sibilantes
items.example: The actor has a slight lisp that is noticeable in some interviews.
items.note: A speech pattern in which sibilant sounds may be replaced by sounds similar to th; a descriptive, not judgemental, term.

items.pt: falar com ceceio
items.example: As a child, he used to lisp when saying certain consonants.
items.note: Verb related to a lisp; distinct from mumbling or speaking quietly.

items.pt: gagueira; bloqueios ou repetições involuntárias na fala
items.example: She explained how her stammer sometimes made public speaking difficult.
items.note: A speech fluency difficulty; British English often uses stammer, with stutter also common.

items.pt: gaguejar
items.example: He sometimes stammers when he is under pressure.
items.note: Can involve involuntary repetitions, prolongations or blocks in speech; not necessarily caused by nervousness.

items.pt: gaguejar; repetir involuntariamente sons na fala
items.example: The presenter stuttered briefly at the beginning of the introduction.
items.note: Close to stammer in ordinary usage; may involve repetitions or difficulty initiating words.

items.pt: falar de modo arrastado; embolar as palavras
items.example: His speech became slurred after the dental procedure.
items.note: Words sound indistinct and run together; can have various causes and does not necessarily indicate alcohol.

items.pt: sem conseguir falar; com a língua travada
items.example: She felt tongue-tied when asked an unexpected question on stage.
items.note: Difficulty finding words because of emotion or nervousness, not necessarily a speech disorder.
